data.name: Korah
data.gender_notes: Korah is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Korah means 'keeper of the sacred places' or 'to be bald'. This name is associated with the Levite leader Korah from the Old Testament, who rebelled against Moses and Aaron. Despite his name meaning 'keeper of the sacred places', Korah's rebellion resulted in his downfall. The name Korah carries the meaning “Levite leader” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Korah usually hope their child will grow to embody levite leader and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reminder to stay loyal to spiritual leaders and uphold faith even in difficult times.
data.etymology: Korah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Levite leader.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Korah total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_latin.name: Core
in_latin.long_meaning: Core est nomen hebraicum quod significat filius Core, Core fuit filius Iezar filius Caath, et fuit unus ex ducibus seditionis contra Mosen, et sic nomen Core symbolizat seditionem et abominationem contra potestatem, sed potest etiam symbolizare independentiam et libertatem

in_english.long_meaning: Korah is a Hebrew name that means son of Korah, Korah was the son of Izhar son of Kohath, and was one of the leaders of the rebellion against Moses, and so the name Korah symbolizes rebellion and abhorrence towards authority, but can also symbolize independence and freedom

data.cultural_impact: The name Korah has been used throughout history in various cultures, most notably in Eastern Europe, where it is a common surname among Jews. It is also found in the Bible and has been the subject of numerous works of art and literature. The rebellion of Korah against Moses and Aaron serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of challenging authority and the potential consequences of pride and ambition.
data.spiritual_significance: Despite his name's association with the sacred, Korah's rebellion against Moses and Aaron illustrates the importance of submitting to God's authority and following His guidance, rather than relying on our own desires and agendas. It serves as a reminder that even those who hold positions of leadership and spiritual responsibility can be susceptible to pride and disobedience, and that we should always strive to keep ourselves aligned with God's will and choose obedience over rebellion.
